answer: An agent market weights votes by locked collateral, not account count, and freezes each deposit for 30 days. A pulse of new identities therefore creates no extra voting power: splitting $1,000 among a thousand agents still buys only $1,000 of weight. The signal is crystal clear: to control a majority, an attacker must lock more collateral than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and paying its financing or opportunity cost throughout the lock.
